text:
ravi: quick RFC follow-up idea we call the plan 'compat ladder' instead of ad-hoc shims. rung 0 = stable v1, rung 1 = bridge proxy, rung 2 = inlined runtime adapters. start with bridge proxy for safety.

claire: bridge proxy handles frame-preserving stream proxying, header translation, and minor payload normalization. downside: extra hop and cache double-touch.

nate: if we inlined hotpaths we avoid double-touch but need migration for KV layout and attention cache format. That migration is risky and needs a compatibility layer anyway.

sara: operational constraints: bridges must expose /health and /ready and include a lightweight metrics facade: compat.lat_ms, compat.frame_drop, compat.quality_alert. Bridge should tag logs with cohort id.

ops-bot: prod-note: bridge-proxy image 95MB, cpu 50m default, mem 128Mi. canary tag pushed to staging.

claire: headers proposed: X-Rwin-Compat-Ladder: rung=1; X-Rwin-Cohort: c-xxxx. prefer header-based opt-in + tenant toggle for admins.

ravi: rollback policy: route-level circuit-breaker -> send to rung0 if p99 latency increase > 25% OR compat.quality_alert > 3 in 10m. Manual override allowed.

nate: owners: bridge impl -> claire, telemetry contract -> ravi, rollout cadence/comms -> sara. I'll draft the KV eviction compatibility checklist.

sara: thanks. plan: prototype bridge this sprint, staging canary next week, customer opt-in in 3 weeks. sync next Tue in #architecture.
